title: Edmund and the Ledger
premise: In the besieged port city of Vhalen, Petra Vane races to complete the master mapmaker's final atlas while imperial census takers catalog every household for conscription and seizure. When census taker Edmund Corliss arrives at the workshop, his one extra question — 'who else has seen these maps?' — marks them both as suspects. Falling in love across the lines of duty, they smuggle the finished atlas out through the flooded catacombs as the workshop burns behind them; Petra escapes to deliver the atlas abroad, carrying Edmund's memory instead of Edmund himself.
about_author: Silas Almeida is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging confiscated maps in coastal municipal libraries before turning to fiction. He writes from a small house above a defunct chart shop, where he still measures everything by what can be carried.

chapters.title: The Weight of Coastlines
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the master's cold workshop, Petra inks the final plates of an atlas that cost him his life, measuring each sheet against what she can carry if orders come. The first census taker passes her door without stopping — but takes the neighbor's son. Emotional beat: grief braided with quiet defiance, the atlas becoming both burden and inheritance.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, shifting briefly to Edmund's. Census taker Edmund Corliss arrives to log the workshop's holdings and asks who else has seen the unfinished maps — then, unsettled by his own question, returns after hours to warn her. Their wary alliance forms over candlelight and ink. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognizing duty's hollowness in each other.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The census bureau flags the atlas for confiscation; Edmund falsifies the ledger to buy Petra three days, knowing it will end him. They plan the route through the flooded catacombs together, love confessed in the space between tides. Climax: soldiers reach the workshop as Petra descends into the dark water with the atlas bound to her chest, Edmund staying behind to burn the duplicates.

chapters.title: Carried
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, epilogue voice. Months later, in a foreign scriptorium, Petra completes the atlas under another name and watches it change hands that will redraw borders. She keeps Edmund's census page — the only record he existed. Emotional beat: sorrow resolved into belonging; she learns that what we carry is not the work but the people the work was for.
